A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Head Pursuit and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Corresponding equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original head-intervention experiments on question answering, toxicity mitigation, image classification, and captioning, including additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their numerical and qualitative outcomes in the main text and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The SOMP decomposition, explained-variance head ranking, and head inversion or amplification procedures are unchanged. The revised auxiliary extractor specification concerns the toxicity experiment's configuration, without a documented change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TriviaQA, RealToxicityPrompts, TET, MNIST, SVHN, EuroSAT, RESISC45, DTD, GTSRB, and Flickr30k. The tasks, targeted concepts, and task-conditioned versus task-agnostic scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Logit Lens and random-head controls retain the same membership in the corresponding main-text and appendix comparisons. The external Llama extractor is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported toxicity-keyword extractor from Llama3.1 to Llama3.3; Appendix E.1 specifies Llama3.1-8B in v1 and Llama3.3-70B in v2. This revises a stated experimental model configuration, although the unchanged prompt and results do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Head-count analyses, cross-dataset head overlap and transfer, task-agnostic classification, amplification-coefficient sensitivity, and qualitative caption examples are retained unchanged, including Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions report random controls over ten independently sampled head sets and retain the same median and interquartile-range reporting. No seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted outcomes, rankings, and substantive qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. In particular, toxicity Tables 2, 7, and 8 retain identical values despite the revised extractor specification.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Section 3, Equations 1–3, and SOMP pseudocode in Appendix A are unchanged. No definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and Section 6 retain the same claims about head specialization, the connection to Logit Lens, and targeted control through interventions on a small fraction of heads.

C2.justification: Interpretations of specialization and targeted intervention effects remain unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations concerning linearity, dictionary quality, coarse interventions, and caption-quality failures in Appendix D.6.

D1.justification: The auxiliary toxicity extractor's documented identity and size change to Llama3.3-70B in Section 4.2 and Appendix E.1. Its prompt remains identical, as do the other checkpoint details, hardware statement, and code-access information. The PDFs do not explain whether this corrects the earlier documentation.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and bibliography are unchanged. The revised Llama model name continues to cite the same reference [40].

P1.justification: Localized wording changes affect Figure 1, Figure 9's caption, the extractor name, and Appendix E.1's heading; the arXiv version/date stamp also updates. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 removes the 'Prompt:' prefix and adds terminal punctuation to an example caption. Figure 9's caption changes 'blue' to 'dark blue' for the 32-head SOMP bars. The diagrams, plotted data, tables, and their placement otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The method, empirical evidence, scientific argument, and limitations remain unchanged. Figure wording receives slight polish, while the auxiliary extractor specification is revised without establishing a correction or an experimental rerun. These limited documentation and presentation edits do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
